PullRequest.Title: sessions: isolate malformed sessions during refresh

## Summary

Prevent a malformed session from interrupting updates and presentation for healthy Agent Host sessions.

Persisted artifacts can contain Windows filesystem paths accepted by older artifact tools. Parsing such a path as a URI treats its drive letter as a scheme; remote URI mapping then throws. Resource-label updates read artifacts across cached sessions, so the exception could interrupt connection setup before session notifications were attached and the listing refreshed. New sessions could remain provisional in the client and disappear on disconnect despite existing on the host.

- Convert persisted absolute Windows drive and UNC paths to file URIs before remote mapping, preserving the artifact and UNC server authority.
- Apply listed sessions independently, including metadata adoption and updates to existing rows. Retain previously seen rows when processing fails rather than interpreting the failure as a deletion.
- Isolate workspace and label-home processing per session so healthy sessions still receive updates, change events, and labels.
- Cover Windows and UNC path recovery, malformed session artifacts, session adoption and updates, healthy workspace and label updates, and reconnect notifications.

The fix is shared by remote providers rather than specific to Mission Control. Related remote artifact mapping: [#336451](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/336451).

## Validation

All of the following passed:

```sh
npm run compile-client
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostSessionArtifacts.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/sessionArtifacts.test.ts --reporter dot
npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/agentHostSessionArtifacts.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostSessionArtifacts.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts
git diff --check
```

The focused unit selection passed 298 tests. Before the original path fix, the Windows artifact regressions reproduced the URI exception. The UNC and session-isolation regressions also failed before their fixes. Tests verify healthy rows before and after a failed row, new session additions, real deletions, preservation of previously seen failed rows, workspace change events, and artifact labels.

Live Mission Control/dev-tunnel flows were not run locally.

### CI

The first head passed every CI job except Linux / Remote, which hit settings-editor click failures also observed on unrelated PRs. The upstream cause was [#341337](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/341337), which replaced the polling editor-focus click with a single 2-second actionability-checked click. [#341393](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/341393) restores the shared helpers. Merged main to pick up that landed fix without adding unrelated smoke changes to this PR, then reran local compilation, lint, and the 298 focused tests successfully.

All six CI workflows passed for merge head `8e16c22b173276a98a87321e2050c38a97d1a1d4`: [Code OSS](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38490326660), [CodeQL](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38490326611), [Monaco Editor checks](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38490326597), [chat-lib tests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38490326714), [Telemetry](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38490326577), and [Component Fixtures](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38490326752). Code OSS includes cross-platform unit, browser, integration, and smoke tests; Linux / Remote passed after the upstream fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial connection or reconnect lists Agent Host sessions, adopts metadata, maps persisted artifacts, and reconciles the session cache.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A single connection.listSessions() request must complete before the provider can sort and synchronously apply the returned catalog; adapter creation/update and artifact URI mapping then run serially before session-change notification. The diff adds per-row failure isolation and Windows-path normalization but no additional awaited work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: connection.listSessions() sends one Agent Host protocol request and returns the full session catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per refresh/reconnect attempt, independent of S; the returned payload contains S sessions. Existing pre-response retry/backoff behavior is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single listSessions request and full-catalog response occurred before the diff; a malformed applied row aborted later in-memory reconciliation rather than adding another boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is on the critical path to authoritative reconciliation; all changed processing occurs after its single response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S listed sessions, with A total persisted artifacts and path-string length P; reconciliation is O(S log S + A*P) on the normal path. Warm reconnect updates cached adapters, while a cold listing creates adapters. Failed rows add one bounded log entry each and are retained rather than aborting the catalog.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The provider permits one refresh in flight via _sessionRefreshInFlight; one list result is processed serially. The diff does not add parallel requests, retries, or a concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold cache creates adapters; warm cache updates existing entries. Persisted cache snapshots are capped at 100 entries, live reconciliation uses exact session keys, and failed listed rows keep their previous warm-cache entry. No cache key, invalidation, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the protocol client shows one listSessions request, and the changed loop is serial in-memory processing. No new boundary or increased normal-path cardinality is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host catalogs can exceed the 100 persisted-entry cap in memory, but typical catalog size and artifact count are not measured here. The only newly broadened work occurs after malformed rows, when later healthy rows now continue processing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Successful rows perform the same work as before; malformed rows now prevent an early abort so later rows are processed, which is required reconciliation work rather than redundant fan-out. Windows path normalization adds only linear string/URI parsing per affected file artifact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workspace labels are recomputed when branch-protection configuration or a remote provider display label changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration/display-name event synchronously scans cached sessions, computes each workspace, collects changed rows, and fires one aggregate event. The diff replaces Array.filter with an equivalent serial loop plus per-session exception handling.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: S cached sessions; one refreshWorkspace computation per session on the healthy path, O(S). If one computation throws, the changed code continues through the remaining sessions instead of aborting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully synchronous and serial on the event callback; no limiter or queue is involved, and the diff does not alter concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the existing in-memory session cache and adapter observables. There are no cold/warm boundary calls, new cache entries, or invalidation changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call sites and refreshWorkspace implementation are in-process, and the changed loop invokes the same method once per healthy session.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of cached sessions and workspace-computation duration are unknown, but the normal-path call count is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The normal-path synchronous cost remains O(S) with identical cardinality; only the malformed-session failure path now completes required work for later sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resource-label homes and artifact label formatters are refreshed on session/draft changes and connection lifecycle events.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The event handler synchronously gathers quick-chat working directories and Copilot CLI artifact homes across known sessions, then updates in-process label formatter registrations. The new try/catch scopes isolate one malformed session without changing healthy-session work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: S known sessions, W working directories, and A artifacts; each refresh is O(S + W + A), with formatter grouping proportional to discovered homes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serial event-handler scan per emitted change; no subprocess, filesystem, network, or IPC work and no changed batching/coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reads existing session/artifact observables and reconciles formatter maps/registrations by key. Existing registrations are reused and removed when absent; the diff does not change ownership or lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced call sites are constructor, connection lifecycle, and session/draft events; formatter updates remain local and keyed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session-change frequency and catalog size vary, but the changed code neither adds events nor repeats the scan beyond existing triggers.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Normal-path scan and registration cardinality are unchanged; continuing after a malformed session adds only the healthy rows that previously lost their labels and does not introduce boundary fan-out or unbounded retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced session listing/reconnect, artifact mapping, workspace refresh, and resource-label refresh. The diff adds failure isolation and bounded path normalization without adding expensive boundaries, increasing healthy-path cardinality, changing concurrency, or creating unbounded state; no performance findings were submitted.
